name: The Millennials Kyoto
detail: I was very satisfied :) First of all, the bedding was really comfortable, and since there were blinds installed, even though it was a dormitory, I could rest comfortably like in a private room. The amenities were also conveniently prepared in various ways. Towels, slippers, toothbrushes, toothpaste, razors, earplugs, shampoo, conditioner, body wash, etc. were available at the front, so I could take as much as I needed and use them comfortably. The shower and restroom were divided into several stalls, so there was almost no waiting while using them. All the staff were friendly, and the lounge had a water dispenser, ice maker, coffee machine, refrigerator, and kitchen facilities, so it was great to be able to prepare simple food myself. The refrigerator was set up so that I could store my items by writing the checkout date, room number, and name, which was convenient. Above all, the location was really good! Not only were there convenience facilities, but the subway and bus stops were also nearby, making it easy to explore Kyoto and come back late. During my stay, all the guests were quiet and respectful, which made for a more comfortable experience. Overall, it was a very satisfying stay. I would love to try other locations as well, not just in Kyoto! 😊

name: GLANSIT KYOTO KAWARAMACHI
detail: All floors have shower rooms available. Each floor has one shower room with a bathtub. The staff are friendly, the facilities are clean, and transport is convenient as the subway and bus are close by, with the market and riverside right in front. A 24 or 25-inch suitcase fits in the locker. You can come back after exploring a place in the morning and take a rest. Many places have restrictions on access during cleaning times for long stays, but there were no such limitations at Glanjit, which was nice. There are water dispensers and microwaves on every floor, and there are vending machines for drinks on the first floor. They provide one large towel and one small towel each day, so there was no shortage. Amenities are available on the first floor, so you can just take what you need. I felt that the staff and the system cared a lot about how it would be for travelers. Thanks to that, I had a great stay in Kyoto.

name: Hotel Elcient Kyoto Hachijoguchi
detail: As soon as I entered the facility, there was a pleasant fragrance, it was clean, and there were plenty of chairs at the front desk. I was satisfied that I could store my luggage both after check-in and after check-out. The amenities were mostly well-prepared, and I was happy that they were also available in the bathroom. The large public bath was spacious and clean, and there were various types of shampoo available, which made me satisfied. The breakfast had a wide variety of food typical of Kyoto, including desserts, and I was happy with it. There was nothing disappointing about this affordable and excellent hotel, and I definitely want to use it again next time. If I had to mention something, it was that since I was on the fifth floor, the view wasn't great.

name: Livemax Hostels Kyoto Ekimae
detail: I often use shared room types of accommodations, and in my opinion, they are highly rated. The bunk beds are individually partitioned like those in a ferry cabin, giving a sense of a small private room, which was quite relaxing. I was on the lower bunk, but the upper bunk had a staircase instead of a ladder, which seemed safer. Whether it was due to soundproofing or everyone's good manners, I hardly heard any noise from neighbors. Additionally, I appreciated that loungewear and towels were provided, and there were more than five women's showers, which always seemed to be available. With an Aeon Mall and convenience store right in front, I could heat up my food in the hotel’s eat-in area and take my time eating. The staff at the front desk were also very friendly, allowing me to relax without worries.

name: APA Hotel Kyoto Ekihigashi
detail: I have stayed at various APA hotels, and this one was conveniently close to the station, which was very helpful as they stored my luggage before and after my stay. The second floor has a small but nice bath made of Kōmeiseki, which helped relieve my fatigue. I opted for breakfast, which included milk and raw eggs, and the food was good. Each guest can have a small serving of three different flavors of gelato, which was very delicious. Since there were many varieties, I wished it was an all-you-can-eat option. The air conditioning near the entrance of the unit bath in the room and in front of the bath had a lot of dust, so I hope they can clean that up soon. Also, there was a strong perfume scent in the room, likely left by a previous guest, which was quite overwhelming until I got used to it. Additionally, when I made my reservation through Agoda, it was booked in romaji, which caused some issues at check-in. The front desk staff kindly re-entered my name into the computer, and I was able to check in successfully. The staff were very courteous when I stored my luggage, which made me feel very relieved. I would love to stay here again when I visit Kyoto.

name: KANSEI Kyoto Hachijo
detail: The price was reasonable, and it was within walking distance from Kyoto Station. The room was also clean. It was nice that check-out was at 11 o'clock. Additionally, both during check-in and check-out, the staff at the front desk were wonderful, and I was able to have a pleasant stay. I would like to stay here again when I go to Kyoto.

name: Sotetsu Fresa Inn Kyoto-Kiyomizu Gojo
detail: You have to walk a bit to the subway station, but it's close to the city center and convenience stores, and the facilities are good. There are enough amenities, which is nice because it allows you to lighten your travel luggage. It was the best among the mid-range business hotels I have visited. The breakfast is decent for 1400 yen. If the prices are reasonable in other areas, I think I will use Sotetsu again next time.

name: Almont Hotel Kyoto
detail: I thought it was a bit far from Kyoto Station, so I had not gone until now, but I finally went! As the title suggests, it is a very good hotel, more than twice as good. It has a large public bath, and the front desk and lobby are very nice, with a sense of cleanliness throughout the hotel. The rooms are also clean, and I was given a spacious room even as a solo guest. There are many affordable and good hotels around Kyoto Station, but you should definitely go to Almont Hotel Kyoto! In fact, I arrived just a short walk away. Choosing to include meals was also a great decision! There are many options that are both convenient and inexpensive, and it is the best hotel around Kyoto Station! It comes highly recommended! The only downside is that I wished there was an outlet by the bedside. It's close to Kyoto Station, has a large public bath, and the rooms are clean, with a great clientele. I will definitely go again.

name: Ace Hotel Kyoto
detail: Directly connected to the station. There are convenience stores and drugstores nearby, and the location is excellent. The staff are friendly, and although the entire hotel is stylish and sophisticated, it has a very calm atmosphere, making it a very comfortable place to stay. We went out for dinner, but next time, I think it would be fine to do everything within the hotel. I also ordered breakfast later, and it was very satisfying! When I come to Kyoto, I would like to stay here again.

name: Natural Hot Spring Dormy Inn Premium Kyoto Ekimae
detail: The location is very close to Kyoto Station, just across the street and a few more steps away. It is really convenient, near Lawson, Starbucks, and a bus stop. The hotel and rooms are fully equipped with amenities and supplies. There is a water dispenser and a coin-operated washing machine available. The breakfast service is packed with quality and there is a lot of food to choose from. If you get the chance, I recommend trying the 1-hour massage service. The massage staff is excellent and helps relieve fatigue very effectively (especially the massage before or after soaking in the onsen, it is truly relaxation -- I want to go back again). The onsen here offers hot and cold water services. Soaking in the extremely cold water as part of Ice-Bathing helps the body recover from various inflammations and promotes recovery very well. It's really great. The rooms are very clean, and the staff is eager to assist. I really like it here.
